CardExtension resolves the app's Progress component defensively and falls back to the core-components Progress when no app context is available.
rules: 1. useProgressComponent is a module-private function (not exported) placed directly above CardExtension, with a short comment saying it falls back to the default progress indicator when the component is rendered outside an app.

2. Its body is a try block that returns useApp().getComponents().Progress and a catch block (no binding) that returns DefaultProgress; the hook is called unconditionally on every render, so the rules of hooks hold.
4. CardExtension calls const Progress = useProgressComponent(); exactly where it called useApp() before, and every existing <Progress /> fallback stays as it is.
5. Nothing else in the file changes; useApp stays imported from '@backstage/core-plugin-api'.

sites.rule: Also import the ComponentType type from 'react': import { ComponentType, useState, Suspense } from 'react';
Import the core-components Progress under the local name DefaultProgress next to InfoCard.
Insert the commented useProgressComponent function of rules 1-3, followed by one blank line.
Replace both lines with the single line const Progress = useProgressComponent();

behaviour: Proves CardExtension renders its title and content, and a progress indicator while lazy content loads, with no app context.
rules: 1. Imports only react, react-dom/client, @backstage/frontend-plugin-api (inside jest.mock) and ./extensions; no @testing-library or @backstage/test-utils import.
2. At the top, jest.mock('@backstage/frontend-plugin-api', () => ({ ...jest.requireActual('@backstage/frontend-plugin-api'), useTranslationRef: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key }) })).

3. Set (globalThis as any).IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true at module level; each test creates a div appended to document.body, renders with createRoot(container) inside act, and in afterEach unmounts the root inside act and removes the div.

4. The lazy case builds Content with lazy() from 'react' over a promise whose resolve the test keeps, uses jest.useFakeTimers() and advances 300 ms inside act so the default Progress becomes visible, then resolves the promise inside an async act; restore real timers in afterEach.
5. Assertions use container.textContent and container.querySelector('[role="progressbar"]'); CardExtension is rendered with title and Content props only.
